We've long warned users not to share sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, as most companies use these conversations as training data — but now there's an even more serious reason.

Over the weekend, things took a drastic turn when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs were accessible through a simple Google search…

Claude chats leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link you can send to one or multiple users, and Claude implicitly assures you that knowing the URL won't allow others to view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered you don't actually need the link to view the conversation. You can simply find it through Google search — either using specific search terms, or by directly instructing Google to show all conversations shared this way. BBC News reports:

You basically just have to tell Google search the directory used for sharing Claude conversations (site:claude.ai/share).

As you'd expect, some of the chat conversations are quite outrageous — for instance, someone asking why the music industry is hiding the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But other conversations contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they need to self-report misconduct; and a user who accidentally published their private keys along with their cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this isn't a problem as of now.

In fact, this is clearly a serious problem, because this is entirely not what users would have expected. Worse still, according to Wired, the root cause appears to be extreme negligence.

This comes just a day after reports that Claude Cowork was able to escape the sandbox environment on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to protect yourself

The problem appears to have been at least partially addressed — search results that were previously accessible no longer work, but given that the sharing feature relies on security by obscurity, I'd recommend avoiding this feature.

I also recommend deleting all conversations you've shared in the past. You can do this in Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage.

Once again proving Apple's approach is superior

Apple has taken a three-tiered approach to privacy protection in Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri:

  • Where possible, AI processing is completed on-device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • Only as a last resort will a Gemini model with equivalent PCC-level protection be used

The extremely sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can access any data whatsoever, nor is any data retained. The security architecture designed by Apple allows independent security researchers to verify this claim.
